title: Message windowing and resume handshake for robust streaming with tool-call alignment
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a pragmatic server-sent-event (SSE) streaming contract focused on: 1) deterministic message/window framing for structured JSONL outputs, 2) an explicit resume handshake that is tolerant to out-of-order fragments, and 3) clear boundaries for tool/function-call envelopes so client libraries can reconstruct and idempotently reapply invocations. This ticket scopes protocol-level changes, server runtime checkpoints, client compatibility shims for legacy SSE consumers, test harnesses, and a canary rollout plan. Goals: reduce user-visible stream corruption on reconnects, guarantee function-call atomicity on resume, and provide a backwards-compatible header-based shim for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits well-formed message windows with contiguous sequence stamps (msg_seq) and fragment indices for any message that spans frames
On reconnect, client can present last-received msg_seq+offset and server resumes without replaying already-acked fragments
Tool/function-call envelopes include a stable call_id and a resume-safe escrow checksum so replayed fragments are detected and handled idempotently
Compatibility shim: when client sends X-Stream-Mode: legacy, server downgrades framing but includes a compat hint stream that allows reconstructors to map to new envelope fields
Automated integration tests cover: mid-message disconnect, duplicate delivery, out-of-order arrival, and partial-function-call reassembly
Metrics show <= 0.1% increase in reconnect-induced application errors in canary region compared to baseline after rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for framing encoder/decoder (msg_seq, fragment_index, fragment_count)
Integration harness simulating jitter, mid-fragment drop, and reorder across HTTP2 and HTTP/1.1 transports
Chaos job to cut connections at controlled offsets and validate client-visible dedup semantics
End-to-end QA with SDKs (js/python/go) verifying function-call reassembly and header shim behavior
Load test to validate checksum/lease overhead at 5k concurrent streams per node
rollout_plan: Merge server PR behind runtime feature flag 'windowed-framing-v1'
Flip on for internal service mesh only and run 48h soak against internal traffic
Canary enable for 1% of hosted API traffic with instrumentation for reconnect error rate and function-call failures
Expand to 25% if metrics are stable for 72h, then 100% after 7 days with rollback playbook ready
Publish migration notes for SDK teams and ship client helpers to read compat hints
comments: 2026-02-11 - Asha Patel: Initial spike complete. PoC demonstrates fragment-indexed windows and resume handshake using a compact 64-bit msg_seq + 32-bit offset. Trade-off: slightly larger per-fragment header but simplifies resume logic.

2026-02-18 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented server-side checkpoint ‘lease’ that ties a msg_seq to an ephemeral lease token. Need security review for token forgery scenarios. Also blocked on SDK changes to propagate X-Stream-Mode header.
2026-02-22 - Riley Chen (SDK): Reviewed envelope shape; requested call_id remain server-assignable when requested by client. Added TODO for ensuring call_id stable across retries from gateway.
2026-02-27 - Security note (Samir Iqbal): Lease tokens should be HMAC-signed with runtime key and TTL <= 30s. Added: security_review_required flag set. Minimal perf impact expected.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Ortega: Added compatibility shim: when client sends X-Stream-Mode: legacy, server sets X-Compat-Hint: map(msg_seq->legacy_offset). This allows older clients to continue operating while SDKs adopt new framing.

2026-03-08 - QA (Priya Rao): Integration harness reproduced a case where a mid-fragment disconnect plus duplicate delivery could cause duplicated function-call side-effects if call_id absent. Confirmed fix by requiring escrow checksum in function envelope.
